input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV.I lets Licensor unilaterally extend the licence for a further seven (7) years at its sole option, with no opt-out right for us and no cap on renewal pricing. That is a multi-year renewal we cannot escape, which sits in walk-away territory under the rule (worse than the fallback of automatic renewal with a ≤60-day non-renewal window and ≤5% uplift). The provision also conflicts with Article IV.II and IV.III, which contemplate extensions only by mutual written agreement. The redline moves the sentence to the preferred position: 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement with uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor-option 7-year renewal with mutual-written-agreement 12-month renewals and a capped uplift
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a seven-year extension exercisable unilaterally by Licensor; our playbook requires renewal only by mutual written agreement (or 12-month automatic renewals we can exit on 30 days' notice), with renewal price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. This also aligns the sentence with Article IV.II and IV.III, which already make extensions subject to mutual written agreement.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for additional periods of twelve (12) months each only by mutual written agreement of the parties, and any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI over the prior period and three percent (3%).
